max_lines.description: The most lines one `read` answer carries; a longer range answers with `more: {from, to}`.

max_chars.description: The most characters of formatted lines one `read` answer carries; beyond it `more` names the next range.

search_limit.description: The most hits one `search` answer lists (`total` counts all of them).

diff_lines.description: The most lines of one `diff`; a longer diff is cut and says `truncated`.

nodes_max.description: The most nodes of a version `outline` computes from its blocks (an older version, a workspace's), and the most one `outline` page can ask for; past it the mark is `truncated`. The same cap as `./derive`, so a computed outline answers like the head's rows.

links_max.description: The most links of a version `links` computes from its blocks, and the most one `links` page can ask for; past it the mark is `truncated`.

extract_max_bytes.description: A version larger than this is not extracted here (mark `too_large`, no nodes).

key_depth.description: How deep the keys of a JSON or TOML file become nodes.

near_scan_max.description: The most file vectors one `near` compares (in id order, so a cut is the same every time).

description.purpose: Every read of the space except `ask`, the semantic search and `dir_summary`: `info` (with the topic `tags` of the version), `read`, `search` (exact, regex), `summary`, `history`, `show`, `diff`, `list`, `find`, `raw`, the node reads (GH #944): `outline` (the items of a version under their anchors, paged by `cursor`/`next`), `links` (its outgoing links, paged alike), `read` of `fh-<12hex>#<anchor>` (the node's lines or page, `unknown_anchor` with up to five candidates of the same name) and `near` (the nearest live files by the Hamming distance of their file vectors, a tie by path; no model), and the directory reads (GH #947): `list` carries each directory's row (`files`, `bytes`, `nodes`, `subdirs`, `dirty`, top `tags`, `summary`) and shows empty directories too, `dir_info` answers one directory with a page of its children by path. It resolves an address (id or path; head, `@<hex>`, `@ws:`, `@snap:`, a prepared commit read all-or-nothing), puts a version together from its blocks and answers with the version token. The head's nodes and links come from the rows `./derive` wrote -- unless the rows fall short of what the run row counts; then, as for any other version, they are computed from its blocks by the same extractors. It never writes a file; its one written table is `pending`.
description.use_when: Inside a file space only, behind `in_read`.
description.not_in_scope: No write, no recovery of a prepared commit (`./ws` does that), no semantic search or directory summary (`./derive`), no node or directory rows of its own (`./derive` writes them), no anchor on any op but `read` (`anchor_unsupported`; a node is written by `./write`).
description.emits_meaning: `read_store` to `./store` between phases, `answer` once per request.
description.consumes_meaning: A request on `in_read`, and the store's answers to its own reads.
